subject.title: [Feature]: cron add: support custom job IDs via --id

question: Should OpenClaw make cron job IDs caller-supplied at creation via a public `cron add --id` and Gateway `cron.add.id` contract, and what validation/collision rules should that contract use?
rationale: This is a new public CLI/API creation field for persisted scheduler identity, so automation can verify the missing behavior but should not choose the permanent ID contract on its own.

options.title: Approve bounded custom IDs
options.body: Add optional create-time IDs with a conservative slug-like validation rule, explicit duplicate rejection, unchanged UUID defaults, docs, and coverage across CLI, Gateway schema, service, and relevant clients.

options.title: Keep UUID-only creation
options.body: Leave create-time IDs server-generated and improve discoverability through listing, display, or name-based workflows instead of adding a new identity field.

options.title: Defer pending broader cron API design
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers decide the larger cron identity/API model, including agent-created jobs and generated-client compatibility.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded custom IDs
recommendation.body: Add optional create-time IDs with a conservative slug-like validation rule, explicit duplicate rejection, unchanged UUID defaults, docs, and coverage across CLI, Gateway schema, service, and relevant clients.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the cron scheduler surface and has the strongest historical ownership signal for a public cron identity contract.
